$comment: A 555 astable (R_A = 1.5 kohm, R_B = 1 kohm, C = 1 uF) on a battery_pack (5 V, 0.9 ohm: the SAP-1's pack) with a 47 uF decoupling capacitor across the rail, clocking a 74LS161 (enabled, never cleared or loaded, powered from the same rail). A clock edge that comes late or is lost shows as a wrong count at the end. 100 ms.

Judged under ruling R122 (a), the handBound marker below: the core against these hand values within the stated bound; classic's distance from them is a divergence row, not a gate (circuit class '555 on a cell's rail': core/README.md, 'The 555 period on a moving rail'). test/core/battery-555-corpus.test.ts also runs the board on both engines at host stops of 100 us, 1 ms and 1/60 s.

By hand (steady rail; thresholds and charge target are both the rail): t_H = ln 2 (R_A + R_B) C = 1.7329 ms; the discharge goes through R_B + (10 ohm in parallel with R_A) = 1009.9 ohm toward u 10 / 1510: t_L = 0.7102 ms (0.693 R_B C alone: 0.6931 ms); period 2.4431 ms, duty 70.93 %. The textbook 0.693 (R_A + 2 R_B) C is 2.4260 ms.

The first HIGH runs from an empty C: ln 3 (R_A + R_B) C = 2.7465 ms. The 555's OUT is high at load, and the counter's clock memory starts LOW, so the counter reads 1 from load (core/spec/w1-classic-semantics.md, 'Initial edges', as fixtures 67 and 73) and adds one at each rise. Rises at 3.4567 ms and every 2.4431 ms: 40 in 100 ms, the last at 98.7371 ms, the next past 100 ms.
Final count: (1 + 40) mod 16 = 9, QD QC QB QA = 1001, with the last rise 1.3 ms before the end and the next 1.2 ms after it.
The rail's sag (the 555 and the counter draw about 10 to 15 mA through 0.9 ohm) moves edges by under 0.1 % of their time; the test's bound is 0.25 % + 5 us, and the count has to be exact.

The rail capacitor's published current is judged at every stop against C dV/dt of the core's own published rail (the right-hand rate), within W0's 1 nA + 1e-3 relative (CAPI, core/README.md Rails point 7: the rail is algebraic and the capacitor follows it; before CAPI the core published 0 there). Classic's readings are recorded beside it, not gated.

handBound.justification: The hand model holds the rail steady; the rail is not. The pack's 0.9 ohm carries a draw that changes with OUT's level (a few mA between the phases, the counter's draw included), so the rail moves a few mV between the phases (under 0.1 %) and the thresholds, which are fractions of the rail, move with it. That shifts an edge by about that fraction of its time (measured worst 0.05 % at the last edge); 0.25 % covers it with margin, and 5 us covers the rail capacitor's own settling (0.9 ohm x 47 uF = 42 us). Classic is judged against the same values and its distance is recorded in the entry's divergence rows, at the app's 1/60 s stops, in numbers: 77 an edge up to 1.4 ms off, a rise lost in 100 ms; 78 up to 1.6 ms, a final count of 8 against 9; 79 a pulse end 0.56 ms late (a step-limited crossing search). So the bound is not set to admit classic.
